capabilities: Receive capture events from the LeetLog browser extension over a local port
Write structured per-problem notes with timing, submission counts and accepted code
Import legacy hand-written notes into a one-file-per-problem format
Configure port, notes folder and note template language (English or Chinese)
Ship ready-made Bases and Dataview dashboard templates
disambiguation: Not a standalone tracker; the plugin is only the receiving bridge — the LeetLog browser extension does the capture and can write notes without Obsidian.
extras: The plugin is one of three interchangeable writers; the extension's folder mode and a Python server work without Obsidian. Cloud sync is in private beta. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: Existing tools push to GitHub, lack timing and attempt history, or send data to a third-party server; the author wanted local-first notes with room for the user's own insights.
problem: Obsidian has no automatic way to capture LeetCode practice sessions — timing, submission counts and accepted code — into local Markdown notes.

relations.evidence: Receives events from the LeetLog browser extension and auto-writes LeetCode practice notes

summary: Bridge plugin that receives events from the LeetLog browser extension and writes LeetCode practice notes with timing, submissions and code into your vault.
